text:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike of CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS errors on serving-runtime-prod (inference pool infer-prod-a). auto-escalation -> incident created IN-2026-045.
monitoring-bot: metric: cuda.illegal_mem_access.rate > 15/min on gpunode-17..20; pod restarts detected: model-server-*-infer (restartCount > 3). logs attached.
monitoring-bot: logs snippet:
```
E TensorRT: Cuda error: an illegal memory access was encountered
W ServingRuntime: misaligned device address in pagewalk at 0x7ff... (GPU 0)
Container crash: SIGSEGV (code=1) - invalid device pointer
```

marta (oncall): I'm paged. Jumping in. Observed cascade: 3 nodes in infer-prod-a showing OOM + illegal mem access, nodes flapping. Moving to live triage.
raj (eng-runtime): I saw a similar trace last month after the kernel backport. Suspect a race in SMMU/pagewalk when buffers are evicted during concurrent KV cache invalidation.
ben (sre): On it. I'll cordon gpunode-17 first to stop new pods landing.
ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon gpunode-17` -> Success.
ben (sre): Draining now with `kubectl drain gpunode-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30` to force pods off. Expect brief capacity loss.
raj (eng-runtime): Recommend toggling backlog route->fallback policy to route traffic away from model-server instances pinned to low-alloc nodes. Can we enable fallback to quantized variant?
marta (oncall): @jordan can you flip routing fallback? We need to reduce pressure and avoid more flaps.
jordan (eng-platform): Routing change planned: switch traffic for route /v1/generate to model:x-quant-1 for 20% of traffic and enable costier but safe CPU fallback for canary customers. Applying now.
ops-bot: Routing update executed: 20% -> model:x-quant-1; 5% CPU-fallback for priority customers.
cs-lead: Heads up: Customer ACME (prod) and BetaCo (stage) reported 500s and truncated responses. Estimated ~1.8% of requests affected in last 12m. Notifying support.
kyle (prod-systems): Adding packet capture and dmesg from gpunode-17 to the incident ticket. Early dmesg shows repeated "GPU0: device address fault at ...".
raj (eng-runtime): If it's the same kernel bug, short-term mitigations: 1) reduce concurrency/batch size on affected nodes, 2) enable eager KV cache pinning to avoid pagewalk at eviction, 3) revert latest cuda/drivers patch on those hosts. Revert risky — need approvals.
ben (sre): Implementing (1) now: scaling down replica sets on infer-prod-a by 25% and patching HPA to cap concurrency. Command: `kubectl scale --replicas=...`
marta (oncall): Noted. Also doing an on-call handoff in 20m to SRE shift lead. Will summarize before I go.
raj (eng-runtime): Quick check: stack trace from crashed container attached. Looks like misaligned address after concurrent release of pinned buffer. Patching model runtime to add fence in KV eviction would help but code change takes >1d. We need live mitigation.
ben (sre): Nodes 17/18 cordoned; 17 drained, 18 still flapping. Starting reboot+driver reload on 18 to clear corrupted driver state.
ops-bot: Command executed: `gcloud compute ssh gpunode-18 -- sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` -> returns ok, reboot scheduled.
jordan (eng-platform): I've temporarily increased routing threshold to prefer Dedicated reserved pool in us-west to absorb load. Should reduce stress on infer-prod-a.
cs-lead: CS running a message to impacted customers: we're aware of increased 500s for a small percentage of requests, mitigation in progress (failover to safe model variant). No data loss. ETA for stable fallback: ~30m. Please confirm if that matches infra.
ben (sre): Confirmed. Re-route completed. Error rate dropping from 15/min -> 4/min after routing changes.
kyle (prod-systems): Collected kernel logs and oops dump uploaded to IN-2026-045. Noted one reproducible event where a container crash preceded a pagewalk error by ~200ms.
sre-shift-lead: I'm taking over oncall from marta in 18 minutes. @marta please post a short summary and outstanding action items.
marta (oncall): Summary: cause suspected misaligned device-address race leading to SIGSEGV in model runtime on GPU nodes. Actions in flight: cordon/drain gpunode-17/18, routing fallback -> model:x-quant-1 and CPU-fallback for priority customers, scale-down replicas on infer-prod-a, reboot/driver reload on gpunode-18. Next: collect kernel oops + coredump, enable extended telemetry, revert driver if repro confirmed.
marta (oncall): Outstanding: eng-runtime to triage root cause and provide a hotfix path (raj), SRE to stabilize fleet and monitor for recurrences (ben/kyle), CS to notify customers (cs-lead). Handoff to @sre-shift-lead in ~10m.
raj (eng-runtime): I'll open a focused PR to add a KV eviction fence and a runtime guard to drop requests that race with buffer release. Will also try to reproduce with stress test (pagewalk + eviction) in staging.
ben (sre): Post-mitigation check: latency normalized for most routes; two small customers still hit by fallback -> CS on it. Marking incident status: partial mitigation: in-progress.
ops-bot: Incident IN-2026-045 updated: status -> "mitigated (partial)"; notes: routing fallback applied; nodes cordoned; reboot in progress; next update in 15m.
cs-lead: Customers updated. No escalations yet. Ticket created for each impacted customer and linked to incident.
sre-shift-lead: Taking over. I'll keep the channel warm and coordinate testing on the rebooted node. If errors persist after driver reload, we'll consider rolling back that kernel backport across infer-prod-a.
marta (oncall): Thanks team. Passing primary to @sre-shift-lead. I'll remain reachable if needed. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Handoff recorded: previous_oncall=marta, new_oncall=sre-shift-lead, time=3332105127
jordan (eng-platform): Plan next: schedule safe rollout of runtime patch behind canary toggles, create test harness for concurrent eviction/pagewalk repro.
raj (eng-runtime): Agreed. Will target canary build within 48h. For now, keep routing fallback and node cordons until we validate kernel/driver behaviour.
ben (sre): Closing note: watch for any new CUDA_ILLEGAL_MEMORY_ACCESS alerts. If rate > 5/min re-elevate to SEV.
monitoring-bot: Alert rate trending down. Incident remains open for follow-up.
